data.one_liner: Flutter SDK for the self-hosted Appwrite backend server
data.what_it_does: Appwrite is an open-source backend-as-a-service client that simplifies complex development tasks behind a REST API. The Flutter SDK integrates apps with Appwrite backend APIs, databases, authentication, and push messaging.
use_when: You are building a Flutter app backed by a self-hosted or Cloud Appwrite server
You need user authentication, database management, and file storage through Appwrite
You need background push messaging delivered directly from Appwrite
avoid_when: You are using a different BaaS provider like Firebase or Supabase
Your app does not communicate with a backend server
strengths: Provides comprehensive access to Appwrite backend services from Flutter
Includes built-in background push notification support for Android
Supports OAuth2 login flows across multiple platforms
weaknesses: Requires careful native configuration for Android minimum SDK, desugaring, and OAuth callbacks
Tied strictly to specific Appwrite server versions
data.setup_notes: Requires platform registration in the Appwrite Console, Android desugaring and build.gradle configuration, and Android manifest activity adjustments for OAuth and push callbacks.

alternatives.name: supabase
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose Supabase if you prefer an open-source PostgreSQL-backed alternative to Appwrite.
